explanation: The winged staff with two snakes is the caduceus of Hermes, messenger of the gods and patron of traders. Its use as a medical emblem, common in the US, is a long-standing mix-up.

claims.text: The Rod of Asclepius shows a single snake coiled around a staff.
Two snakes with wings is the caduceus, a snake around a bowl is the Bowl of Hygieia, and a snake eating its tail is the ouroboros.
The caduceus, a winged staff with two snakes, is the staff of Hermes.
Hermes was the messenger of the gods and a patron of merchants.
The caduceus is often used as a medical symbol, especially in the United States, although the traditional symbol of medicine is the Rod of Asclepius.
